engagement.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture against patient-derived and site-directed Gag-polymorphic viruses, with in-vitro resistance selection

The viral-load decline (Hwang 2017) is the earliest human PD signal but is assigned to dose and efficacy rather than reused here. registry_date is the NCT01803074 results posting; the resistance comparison itself was first public in this 2019 paper (epub 2019-10-17).

engagement.reason: Same Gag site selected in culture and patients
engagement.judgement: Strengthening entry for a second member (fipravirimat); year is the AAC epub (2021-11-15), registry_date the NCT03784079 results posting. Spinner 2022 adds the cross-member count: of 37 GSK3532795 monotherapy participants with data, 18 had emergent RAMs and 6 A364A/V, 5 with phenotypic resistance. The emergence drove a protocol amendment shortening monotherapy to 7 days, after which no RAMs appeared.

Its PD readout (CA-SP1 cleavage in infected thymocytes) is direct. No PubMed record reports GSK3532795, GSK3640254 or GSK2838232 in any humanized mouse, so the track stays untested; the paper's own side-by-side with bevirimat 10-day monotherapy patients (resistance absent in both) is a non-member comparison and is not scored. dose.model: Protein-binding-adjusted cell-culture EC90 (40% human serum + albumin) as the plasma trough target
dose.note: Serum shift 5.4-fold (86% bound) gave a protein-adjusted EC90 of 14 nM for BMS-955176; the patient trough target was derived from it.

dose.quote: A 5.4-fold reduction in EC50 occurred in the presence of 40% human serum plus 27 mg/ml of human serum albumin (HSA), which corresponded well to an in vitro measurement of 86% human serum binding.
dose.judgement: The dose track is the same cell system read as a serum-adjusted potency; it opens in 2016 with the first member paper rather than 2009 because the bevirimat-era serum-shift work is not a member source and the 643 ng/mL target was formalised for GSK3532795. Nowicka-Sans 2016 also cites the Phase 2a result as unpublished data; the scored comparison is taken from the trial paper (Hwang 2017). No NOAEL or tolerability margin is public for any member (no FDA review), so margin_stated is null throughout.

dose.model: Protein-binding-adjusted cell-culture EC90 (40% human serum + albumin) as the plasma trough target
dose.note: Antiviral response plateaued at C24 >=500 ng/mL, close to the 643 ng/mL protein-adjusted target trough; every dose >=40 mg cut HIV RNA >1 log10.
dose.short: Plateau at trough matches protein-adjusted target
dose.quote: The plateau in antiviral response observed at GSK3532795 C24 ≥500 ng/mL is consistent with protein-binding adjusted target Ctrough of 643 ng/mL, representing plasma concentrations that are expected to provide coverage of >90% of subtype B viruses
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. Quote is the first 36 words of a longer sentence (it continues ', which includes the ∆V370 genotype...').
dose.magnitude_basis: trough at the antiviral plateau (>=500 ng/mL) vs protein-adjusted target trough (643 ng/mL)
dose.judgement: Called 'same' because the exposure at which response plateaued sits within 2x of the serum-adjusted target and all doses above it were active. Caveat recorded, not scored: in the Phase 2b (Morales-Ramirez 2018, 10.1371/journal.pone.0205368; NCT02415595 results 2018-09-19) 'the AE and efficacy endpoints did not show strong trends with increasing GSK3532795 exposure' across 60-180 mg, and the trial was terminated for GI intolerability and NRTI-backbone resistance (M184V/I in 10/12 sequenced failures), so the exposure model could not rank doses and may have under-called the antiviral pressure needed to protect the backbone. The Week-24 primary endpoint was met, so this is not a dose failure under the table; the harm is scored in safety.

dose.reason: Target trough held; 100-150 mg matched DTG
dose.judgement: Strengthening entry for the second member. Magnitude is direction_only because PK was non-proportional between 140 and 200 mg and the response had not plateaued, so the target cannot be placed within 2x. The Phase 2b doses (100/150/200 mg) were then chosen by exposure-response modelling to keep troughs >3x PBA EC90 (0.11 ug/mL) in >95% of participants (Joshi 2025, 10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103567); 100 and 150 mg matched dolutegravir at Week 24, which is consistent with the target but is recorded under efficacy rather than as another dose entry.

dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The exposure statement is for bevirimat (non-member); no member exposure target was ever set from this model.

The members' exposure targets came from the serum-shifted cell panel (draft track hiv-gag-polymorph-cell-panel).
dose.model: HIV-1-infected SCID-hu Thy/Liv humanized mouse (human fetal thymus/liver implant), oral dosing, thymocyte viral RNA, p24 and CA-SP1 cleavage

dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC5848258); 'C24' and 'log10' are subscripts in the original. Opening entry: the model's prediction (no gain above the plateau) had not yet been tested in a separate trial.

dose.judgement: A distinct system from the draft's serum-shifted EC90 target: the exposure-response model is fitted to patient viral loads, then used prospectively to choose the Phase 2b regimen (205891 chose 60/120/180 mg, all above the plateau). Fitted-to-same-patients models are excluded elsewhere in the atlas when they predict nothing new; this one made a prospective regimen prediction that a later trial tested. Registry NCT01803074 results posted 2019-11-25, after the paper.
dose.model: Population PK + sigmoid Emax exposure-response model fitted to Phase 2a monotherapy viral-load data, with clinical-trial simulation, used to pick Phase 2b doses

dose.magnitude_basis: Week-24 HIV-1 RNA <40 copies/mL across 60-180 mg (76-83%) vs the Phase 2a prediction of no additional response above C24 >=500 ng/mL
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC6198970). Paired by me: the Phase 2b paper reports the flat exposure-response but does not itself cite the Phase 2a Emax plateau as the prediction. The regimen was later abandoned for GI intolerability and NRTI-backbone resistance (rule question 3); dose stays same because the exposure target was reached and the Week-24 primary was met.
dose.note: Phase 2b at 60/120/180 mg (all above the plateau) gave 76-83% <40 copies/mL vs 77% on efavirenz, with no exposure-response, as the plateau model predicted.
dose.quote: Efficacy endpoints demonstrated little correlation to GSK3532795 exposure. It is likely that lower doses would need to be studied to elucidate clear exposure-response relationships.
dose.judgement: Model predicted that doses above the plateau would add nothing; Phase 2b found exactly that (little correlation of efficacy with exposure) and the primary endpoint was met at every dose. Scored same, direction only, because the model gave no response-rate prediction. The model may also have placed the plateau too low to be useful for dose discrimination (the authors say lower doses would be needed to see a relationship), which is a limitation, not a contradiction. Year is the registry results posting (2018-09-19); paper epub 2018-10-23.
dose.model: Population PK + sigmoid Emax exposure-response model fitted to Phase 2a monotherapy viral-load data, with clinical-trial simulation, used to pick Phase 2b doses

The paper states the doses were selected on the basis of clinical trial simulations via population PK and exposure-response modeling, with >=100 mg predicted to exceed the 75% threshold. DOMINO (NCT04493216, results 2023-11-18) used the same simulation-selected doses with two NRTIs and matched dolutegravir (draft efficacy track).

The simulation predicted all three doses on the plateau; 100 and 150 mg met the prespecified Week-24 threshold and 200 mg did not (77%, with protocol-defined virologic failure and more GI events), so source_calls_it is partial and the entry stays same (target reached and enough at two of three doses). Year follows the draft's convention for DOMINO: the registry results posting (2023-12-14) is the earliest public patient result; the stated comparison itself is in the 2025 paper (epub 2025-10-17). dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC9965536). The model was developed, qualified and verified on the same healthy-volunteer fasted/fed data it reproduces (NCT03231943 FTIH, NCT04263142 food effect), so this is a retrodiction; the fasted-state profile was over-predicted with conventional media. No prospective use of the model (e.g. a new formulation or meal) was found. First author (Stamatopoulos) and epub date (2023-02-03) verified on the PubMed record.

dose.quote: Thus, by using Simcyp® v20 software, the PBBM model accurately predicted the results of the food effect and predicted data were within a two-fold error with 70% being within 1.25-fold.
dose.judgement: In-silico track under the brief's 'in-silico models used to choose doses' category: the model supports the take-with-food regimen used in Phase 2b (DYNAMIC/DOMINO dosed with a low-fat meal). Scored retro, never same, because the clinical food effect (Spinner/Johnson food-effect study, 3-4-fold) was known before the model was built (decision 10). Opens and is compared in the same year, so no separate untested entry. Registry date is the food-effect study results posting (NCT04263142, 2021-03-03), the patient-side datum the model reproduces.

Qualitative statement only; no predicted human clearance or dose number is given, and the sponsor relied on it to skip urine collection ('preclinical evaluation indicated negligible renal excretion'). Pending rule question 4 (whether a cross-species ADME projection is a model-system track); drop this track if the rule says no. Species not named for the ADME work (6-month rat and 9-month dog are the chronic tox species).

dose.quote: Metabolite profiles observed preclinically were qualitatively similar to those observed in human plasma.
dose.judgement: Placed under dose because the projection set the regimen: predicted CYP3A4-driven clearance translated into the ritonavir-boosted regimen that reached ~8x PA-IC90 at 200 mg + RTV (Johnson 2018), and predicted negligible renal excretion set the clinical sampling plan. The Phase 1 registry records (NCT02289495, NCT02795754) carry no posted results. Checker listed this as a candidate pending a rule decision; kept apart from mi-nonclinical-tox because it predicts disposition, not harm.

The abstract also states fraction absorbed 0.26, gut escape 0.898 and hepatic extraction 0.00544 were 'all consistent with low in vitro intrinsic clearance in liver microsomes and hepatocytes'. First author (Wen B, epub 2022-09-24) verified on the PubMed record; registry record for the mass-balance study not identified.

dose.short: Human ADME matched in-vitro clearance prediction
dose.quote: No major metabolites in human plasma required further qualification in animal studies.
dose.judgement: Second member on the track; strengthening entry, status unchanged. The human study confirmed the unboosted once-daily regimen's basis (low intrinsic clearance, 21.7 h half-life) and that animal metabolite exposure covered every human metabolite (ICH M3 qualification). Same caveat as the 2018 entry: pending rule question 4.

efficacy.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture against patient-derived and site-directed Gag-polymorphic viruses
efficacy.note: Cell-culture replication of patient-derived viruses carrying Gag polymorphisms: bevirimat failed on polymorphic viruses, so the panel became the class's efficacy screen.
efficacy.short: Polymorphic-virus panel is the efficacy screen
efficacy.quote: We found that reduced BVM susceptibility was associated with naturally occurring polymorphisms at positions 6, 7, and 8 in Gag spacer peptide 1.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Bevirimat is a non-member proxy that opens the strip and scores nothing.
efficacy.judgement: No animal efficacy model exists for this class: HIV-2 and SIV Gag are intrinsically resistant to GSK2838232 (Jeffrey/Smith 2023, 10.1371/journal.pone.0280568), so no macaque arm was possible and the class went to patients on cell culture alone. The cell is therefore a populated track, not an empty list.

efficacy.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture against patient-derived and site-directed Gag-polymorphic viruses
efficacy.note: Ten-day GSK3532795 monotherapy cut HIV RNA >1 log10 at every dose >=40 mg, in subtype B and C, and irrespective of the Gag polymorphisms that defeated bevirimat.
efficacy.quote: Median of the maximum declines in HIV-1 RNA were similar for the 40–120 mg once-daily dose groups regardless of baseline Gag polymorphisms.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. Primary endpoint was change in HIV-1 RNA to day 11 (registry).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: antiviral activity across Gag genotypes; cell-culture EC50s do not predict the size of the log10 drop

patient_trials.quote: A >1 log10 median decline in HIV-1 RNA was achieved by day 11 in parts A and C and day 29 in part B at GSK3532795 doses ≥40 mg
At Week 24, 76-83% participants receiving GSK3532795 and 77% receiving EFV achieved HIV-1 RNA <40 copies/mL.

efficacy.judgement: The panel predicted activity across the polymorphisms that defeated bevirimat and the 10-day monotherapy confirmed it; comparison_stated because the paper reads the subtype C and polymorph results against the in-vitro susceptibility profiles. Partial patient-level caveat: Dicker 2022 notes that Phase 2a participants carrying the more complex V362I/V370A combination responded less, which the panel had listed among reduced-susceptibility genotypes, so the patient-level prediction is directionally right but was not pre-specified. The Phase 2b (NCT02415595) met its Week-24 primary (76-83% vs 77% on efavirenz) yet was terminated for GI intolerability and NRTI-backbone resistance; that is a safety/regimen failure, not an efficacy miss, so the status does not change. 'neg' is unavailable: no member fell below the class bar in the model. GSK2838232 Phase 2a (DeJesus 2020, 10.1093/cid/ciz938, abstract only; NCT03045861 results 2019-05-29; -1.70 log10 at 200 mg + cobicistat) is a consistent third member not given its own entry.

efficacy.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture against patient-derived and site-directed Gag-polymorphic viruses
efficacy.note: Fipravirimat Phase 2b: Week-24 HIV RNA <50 c/mL in 83-91% on 100-150 mg + 2 NRTIs vs 92% on dolutegravir (DOMINO); 95%/85% vs 86% as a two-drug regimen with DTG (DYNAMIC).
efficacy.quote: The efficacy in the GSK'254 100-mg and 150-mg groups more closely matched the efficacy in the DTG group at Week 24 (83% and 91% vs 92% response rates, respectively) and were therefore consistent with efficacy expected of contemporary antiretroviral agents.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The 200 mg arms underperformed (76-77%) through AE discontinuations (DOMINO) and blips (DYNAMIC); both trials were stopped early by company decision (registry: 'not based on any safety or efficacy concerns'), so no Week-48/96 primary data exist.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: Week-24 Snapshot suppression vs the model's prediction of broad-spectrum activity (PBA EC90 33 nM across the polymorph library)

patient_trials.quote: The efficacy in the GSK'254 100-mg and 150-mg groups more closely matched the efficacy in the DTG group at Week 24 (83% and 91% vs 92% response rates, respectively)

At Week 24, proportions with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL were 95% (21/22), 85% (17/20), and 77% (17/22) in the GSK'254 100-mg, 150-mg, and 200-mg groups, respectively, vs 86% (18/21) in the DTG plus 3TC group.

efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: the model side is Dicker 2022 (library-wide PBA EC90 33 nM, clinical-isolate EC50 9 nM) and the trial side the two Phase 2b papers; the trial papers cite the model work but do not compare to it, hence comparison_stated false. Year is the NCT04493216 results posting (2023-11-18), the earliest both sides were public; the papers are 2025. The 200 mg arms' lower Snapshot rates are attributed by the authors to missing data and blips, not to loss of antiviral effect, so the status is same, not partial. ViiV stopped fipravirimat for portfolio reasons (registry whyStopped) and an editorial (10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103573) reads the decision as commercial; no member of this class has failed an efficacy endpoint in patients.

efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read; quote as printed in the PubMed abstract ('log(10)'). Proxy compound only.
efficacy.note: Oral bevirimat cut thymocyte viral RNA >2 log10 and spared T cells; SP1/A1V resistance reproduced in vivo. No member drug tested.
efficacy.short: Bevirimat >2 log10 drop in SCID-hu mice
efficacy.quote: Oral administration of bevirimat to HIV-1-infected SCID-hu Thy/Liv mice reduced viral RNA by >2 log(10) and protected immature and mature T cells from virus-mediated depletion.
efficacy.judgement: Withdraws the draft's claim that no animal efficacy model exists for the class: this one did, was cited as ref 52 of Nowicka-Sans 2016, and was not used (or not published) for any second-generation member. Untested rather than empty because the model existed and was used for the class's first-generation compound. HIV-2/SIV Gag is intrinsically resistant (Zhou 2004 Retrovirology; Yang 2023 PLoS One doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0280568), which rules out macaques but not humanized mice.

safety.model: Nonclinical toxicology (short- and longer-duration repeat-dose studies; species not public)
safety.note: GSK2838232: short-duration tox raised minimal, sporadic cardiovascular signals not reproduced in longer studies; Holter/troponin-monitored Phase 1 found no drug-related cardiovascular toxicity.
safety.short: Equivocal animal CV signal; humans clean
safety.quote: Sporadic cardiovascular events were seen on active and placebo arms, and none were considered definitively related to GSK2838232.
safety.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The nonclinical signal was itself equivocal ('minimal, appeared sporadically, and were not reproduced in longer term studies'); scored as the longer-term prediction holding. A reader could instead treat the short-term signal as a predicted harm that never appeared. Species and exposures are not public (no FDA review).
safety.magnitude_basis: cardiovascular events on drug vs placebo in 124 healthy subjects across four Phase 1 studies
safety.judgement: The only public animal-side safety statement for any member before 2025. The paper juxtaposes the nonclinical signal with intensive cardiovascular monitoring in Phase 1, so comparison_stated is true; one SAE 'of a cardiovascular nature' terminated one study early and was later judged unlikely to be drug-related. Not scored on this track: the harm that killed BMS-955176 (GI disorders in 65% vs 30% on efavirenz; diarrhoea 27-51% by dose; Morales-Ramirez 2018) has no public animal-side record, so the model's silence or prediction on it cannot be judged. The Phase 1 registry records (NCT02289495, terminated; NCT02795754, completed) carry no posted results, so registry_date is null and the comparison was first public in this paper. GSK2838232 was later shelved for its boosting requirement (editorial 10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103573), not for safety.

safety.model: Nonclinical toxicology (short- and longer-duration repeat-dose studies; species not public)
safety.note: Fipravirimat animal tox predicted gastric parietal/chief-cell changes; paired Week-24 gastric biopsies in DOMINO (14 on drug) showed no drug-related findings and gastrin/pepsinogens were unchanged.
safety.short: Animal gastric lesions absent in patient biopsies
safety.quote: At Week 24, following pathology evaluation of gastric biopsies, there were no drug-related microscopic findings.
safety.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. Only 17 paired biopsies (14 on GSK3640254) at 24 weeks; the planned Week-96 biopsies never happened because the trial was stopped. The animal exposure at which the gastric changes occurred is not public, so the model may have placed the finding above clinical exposure, in which case this is a margin that held rather than a miss.
safety.magnitude_basis: predicted gastric parietal/chief-cell changes vs paired Day-1/Week-24 gastric biopsies and serum gastrin, pepsinogen I/II
safety.reason: Animal gastric lesions absent in patient biopsies
safety.judgement: Scored under the v3 rule that a predicted harm which never appeared in patients is contra with magnitude opposite: the sponsor ran a prospective EGD sub-study specifically 'to look for evidence of translation of non-clinical toxicology findings (eg, parietal cell and chief cell changes)' and found none. Confidence is low for the reasons in confidence_note; a checker who weighs the unknown exposure margin may downgrade to same with margin_stated. Year is the paper (epub 2025-10-17); the registry results posting (2023-11-18) was not checked for the exploratory biopsy endpoint. Clinical GI intolerability with fipravirimat was 29-42% vs 31% on dolutegravir in DOMINO and higher in the 150/200 mg DYNAMIC arms; the GI harm of the class was addressed by chemistry (reduced basicity), not predicted by an animal model. GSK3640254's thorough-QT study (10.1002/prp2.1151: ddQTcF 10.6 ms at a 500 mg supratherapeutic dose) has no public animal-side counterpart and is not scored.
